description: The plot titled “Hidden State Mean” illustrates how the absolute mean (“Abs Mean”) of hidden states varies across network layers for three conditions: before a gate, after a gate, and a baseline. The x-axis is labeled “Layer,” uses a linear scale, and spans approximately layers 0 through 23 with labeled ticks at 0, 5, 10, 15, and 20. The y-axis is labeled “Abs Mean,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from about 0 up to a little above 4 (with labeled ticks at 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4). The first line is a blue dashed line (legend: “hidden state mean before gate, avg 0.71”) that starts near 0 at layer 0, rises to roughly 0.2–0.3 by around layers 2–3, stays around ~0.2–0.5 through the mid layers, then increases more sharply after about layer 18, reaching around ~0.9 near layer 19–20, jumping to roughly ~2.6 around layer 21–22, and ending near ~4.4 at the final layer. The second line is an orange dotted line (legend: “hidden state mean after gate, avg 0.05”) that stays close to 0 across layers, gradually increasing from near 0 at early layers to around ~0.05–0.1 by the final layers, with only small fluctuations. The third line is a green solid line (legend: “hidden state mean of baseline, avg 0.04”) that also remains near 0 throughout, starting near 0 at layer 0 and slowly rising to roughly ~0.08–0.1 by the last layer, tracking a gentle upward trend with minimal variation.
